correctness.rationale: All thresholds U_t are tested in the endpoint proof, including empty and total opens. The all-or-none empty-row dichotomy and powers-of-two interior choices are exact. The interval subclass has a reversible two-row tableau encoding and a standard verified hook-content evaluation. For fixed target size m>=3, the unique maximal row weight has a simple dominant pole; the factorization into left and right anchored endpoint chains gives the exact coefficient C_m, and all remaining poles have at most half its modulus. A standalone checker exhaustively compared independent modal and endpoint conditions on 74,954 binary relations, matched weighted counts, and tested rational constants. The general result is proved symbolically; finite checks do not certify infinite parameter ranges.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 modal duality paper introduces the continuity class but not its counts. Barmak–Mrozek–Wanner (2018, Lemma 3.2) subsumes the qualitative semicontinuity criterion, explicitly acknowledged as prior; classical hook-content theory subsumes the interval-valued tableau count. The new single object of evaluation is the exact *unrestricted* weighted relation census and its explicit dominant-pole constant/universal quarter-law, neither found in the inspected full primary texts or targeted research records. value.rationale: This completes the natural enumeration of *all* binary modal relations whose box and diamond predicate transformers preserve Alexandrov opens on every finite chain pair. The unrestricted row interiors produce a nontrivial weighted two-row tableau statistic absent from the classical interval/SSYT census. The sharp dominant-pole analysis identifies an exact asymptotic leading constant and an unexpected universal 4^{-r} density for fixed target size >=3. The full diagonal counts are natural benchmark invariants in modal relational semantics. No external general theorem or paper-sized contribution is asserted.
